title: Adamu and the Lights Left On

pages.text: One evening, an alert came on Adamu’s mother’s phone: their prepaid electricity units were almost finished. “Already?” Mama sighed. “We bought units only two weeks ago.” Adamu frowned thoughtfully. “Let us find out why.” His friend Gadzekpo agreed to help.
sentences: One evening, an alert came on Adamu’s mother’s phone: their prepaid electricity units were almost finished.
“Already?” Mama sighed.
“We bought units only two weeks ago.” Adamu frowned thoughtfully.
“Let us find out why.” His friend Gadzekpo agreed to help.
pages.alt: On a warm Ghanaian evening veranda, Adamu’s mother looks surprised at her glowing mobile phone while Adamu and Gadzekpo look on with a plain notebook.

pages.text: Next afternoon, they walked around the house checking each room. A bulb shone in an empty bedroom, a fan spun with nobody inside, and the television played to an empty sofa. On a table sat an iron left plugged in! “Do not touch it,” warned Gadzekpo wisely. “Tell Mama right away, because it could start a fire.”
sentences: Next afternoon, they walked around the house checking each room.
A bulb shone in an empty bedroom, a fan spun with nobody inside, and the television played to an empty sofa.
On a table sat an iron left plugged in!
“Do not touch it,” warned Gadzekpo wisely.
“Tell Mama right away, because it could start a fire.”
pages.alt: Inside a tidy Ghanaian living room, Adamu and Gadzekpo stand safely back and point toward a lit bulb, a spinning fan, an unwatched television, and a plugged-in iron.

pages.text: After Mama safely unplugged the iron, the children made a plan: switch off lights and fans when leaving a room, open curtains to use daylight, unplug televisions and chargers when not in use, and iron many clothes at once rather than one by one. “And use energy-saving LED bulbs!” added Adamu.
sentences: After Mama safely unplugged the iron, the children made a plan: switch off lights and fans when leaving a room, open curtains to use daylight, unplug televisions and chargers when not in use, and iron many clothes at once rather than one by one.
“And use energy-saving LED bulbs!” added Adamu.
pages.alt: At a sunlit wooden table, Adamu and Gadzekpo draw neat wordless picture icons of a light bulb, fan, sunbeam, and clothes iron in a plain sketchbook.

pages.text: “Safety comes first,” said Adamu’s mother. “Always dry your hands before touching a light switch. Never poke anything into a socket, never touch a loose wire, and let grown-ups handle plugs and irons.” Both children promised carefully.
sentences: “Safety comes first,” said Adamu’s mother.
“Always dry your hands before touching a light switch.
Never poke anything into a socket, never touch a loose wire, and let grown-ups handle plugs and irons.” Both children promised carefully.
pages.alt: Adamu’s mother dries her hands on a clean towel beside a wall switch while demonstrating electrical safety to attentive Adamu and Gadzekpo.

pages.text: Each Sunday, Adamu stood with Mama to read the prepaid meter and record the electricity units used. In week one, the household used 18 units. After practising their new habits, they used only 13 units in week two! “We saved five units in just one week!” cheered Adamu.
sentences: Each Sunday, Adamu stood with Mama to read the prepaid meter and record the electricity units used.
In week one, the household used 18 units.
After practising their new habits, they used only 13 units in week two!
“We saved five units in just one week!” cheered Adamu.
pages.alt: Beside a grey household meter box on the veranda wall, Mama points up while Adamu records tally marks in his plain notebook and Gadzekpo smiles.

pages.text: “Conserving electricity saves our family money,” said Gadzekpo. “It also helps the environment and shares power fairly across our community.” Mama smiled proudly. “You have taught the whole house.” Together they taped their picture checklist beside the front door.
sentences: “Conserving electricity saves our family money,” said Gadzekpo.

pages.alt: Mama tapes the children’s wordless picture chart of light-bulb and sunbeam icons beside the front door while Adamu and Gadzekpo beam with pride.

activities.question: Which habit helps conserve electricity at home?
options: Switching off lights and fans in empty rooms
Leaving the clothes iron plugged in
Running the television with nobody watching

activities.question: Who should handle wall plugs and hot clothes irons?

activities.prompt: Put the family’s electricity-saving investigation in order.
items: The prepaid electricity units nearly ran out.
Adamu and Gadzekpo spotted wasted power around the house.
They made a safe plan to conserve electricity.
Weekly meter readings showed fewer units used.
